info.title: Unify Compute dashboard API
info.description: The /dashboard/v1 routes the dashboard pages call (ADR-0011, docs/spec/accounts.md). Served by compute-api only with ACCOUNTS_BACKEND=local and only on the app host (Host = APP_ORIGIN's host, else 404); with the console backend none of it exists. Not part of the job API contract (compute-api/internal/api/openapi.json): no API key is accepted here and no cookie there. Every non-GET needs Origin = APP_ORIGIN; session routes need the __Host-uc_session cookie and, for non-GET, X-CSRF-Token. compute-api/internal/dashboard tests hold this document's operations against the registered routes. Balance, history, usage and the account's jobs (A7d) reuse the job API's objects by reference to openapi.json; Card top-ups and the Stripe webhook (B1) are here; export and close are not yet.

post.description: Checks the account's limits (ADR-0011 D4: USD 10 to 100 per top-up, available plus held at most USD 200 afterwards, at most 3 top-ups that were not abandoned in any 24 hours; the operator can raise them per account), records an open top-up and creates a Stripe Checkout Session for it: mode payment, one USD line item for the amount, cards only, no saved payment method, the top-up id as client_reference_id and idempotency key, metadata product=unify-compute, account_id, topup_id and environment, expiring after one hour. The page sends the browser to checkout_url (a full redirect; no Stripe script runs on our pages). Stripe sends the customer back to /billing?topup=<id>&checkout=success or =cancelled. Nothing is credited here or on that return: only the webhook credits. If the account already has an open top-up, its Checkout Session is expired at Stripe first, so it can no longer be paid; if Stripe says it was already paid, the answer is 409 topup_open. At most 10 requests that pass validation per account per hour. Writes a topup_created audit event.

The message invites the customer to contact us for a review.

post.summary: Ask for a refund of a top-up to its card
post.description: Records a refund request and emails the operator (ADR-0013 §2). Nothing is refunded here: the operator refunds to the original card with `admin topup refund`, and the refund, once Stripe's charge.refunded is applied, closes the request and emails the customer; or the operator declines it with a message that is emailed. amount_usd defaults to everything still refundable. A refund takes its share of the top-up's bonus with it and must fit in the unused balance; the operator checks that. Writes refund_requested. At most one open request per top-up; 5 requests per account per 24 hours. Owners and admins only.

post.description: Called by Stripe, server to server: no session, no CSRF header and no Origin check, still only on the app host. The credential is Stripe-Signature over the raw body (at most 256 KiB): HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>" under the endpoint's signing secret (STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET), compared in constant time with every v1, and t within 5 minutes of our clock either way. Handled: checkout.session.completed with payment_status paid and checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded (credit), checkout.session.async_payment_failed (failed), checkout.session.expired (expired); charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created and charge.dispute.closed on a compute top-up are stored and not yet applied (B2). A credit happens once per top-up, in one transaction with the stripe_events row (unique on the event id), a topup balance entry (idempotency key topup:<id>) and a topup_credited audit row, and only if the session matches the top-up exactly (session id, account, amount, currency usd, mode payment). The Stripe account is shared with Unify API: every event that is not compute's (no metadata.product=unify-compute or another environment on a Checkout Session; a charge or dispute whose PaymentIntent is no top-up's; the other mode; any other type) is answered 200 and not stored, so Stripe neither retries it nor marks the endpoint failing.

200.description: Verified. outcome: credited, already_credited, expired, failed, awaiting_payment, no_change, recorded, rejected (compute's own event that does not match its top-up; never credited, logged as an error), duplicate (event seen before) or ignored (not compute's).

At most 10000 rows; ask for a shorter period beyond that. Product-design task C10.

session.name: __Host-uc_session
session.description: Host-only, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax. Idle 12 h, absolute 7 d. Non-GET requests also send X-CSRF-Token with the csrf_token from login, verify or /me.

name.description: How the tenant appears in the dashboard and member emails. The first user's email until renamed.

param.description: The field to show the message under; absent for the form-level box.

Key.description: An API key's metadata. The secret is never part of it.

id.description: The key id; DELETE /keys/{id} takes it, and jobs record it as the key that submitted them.

display.description: `uck_` and the first 8 characters of the secret, to recognise the key by.

scopes.description: `jobs`: submit, cancel and read jobs, events, logs and artifacts. `read`: read only. Always in the order jobs, read.

last_used_at.description: Unix seconds of the last job API request, to within a minute; null if never used.

revoked_at.description: Unix seconds; null while not revoked.

monthly_cap_usd.description: The key's spending cap per UTC calendar month; null is no cap. A job whose hold would take the key past it is refused with 403 key_cap_exceeded (job-api.md).

spent_this_month_usd.description: What the key's holds this UTC month amount to: open holds at their full amount, closed ones at what they settled. The figure the cap is checked against. Null when this deployment has no local ledger.

CreatedKey.description: The key just created, with its secret. This is the only response that ever carries the secret.

secret.description: The whole key, for `Authorization: Bearer` on the job API. Shown once; only its SHA-256 is stored.

held_usd.description: Reserved for running jobs; what a job does not use comes back when it ends.

low_balance_usd.description: The low-balance warning's threshold (default 5.00; 0.00 is off). The dashboard shows a banner while available_usd is below it, and the account's owners get one email each time available drops below it (again only after a top-up or credit brings it back to the threshold or more).

amount_usd.description: The one figure a history row shows: for settle, the charge taken out of held (negative); for every other kind, the change in available.

job_id.description: The job a hold, extend, settle or release belongs to; null otherwise.

ref.description: What caused the entry, when the account holder can see it; null for an operator adjustment.

detail.description: sku, for entries that belong to a hold. Nothing else, and never an operator's reason.

next.description: Present when has_more: the last entry's id, to pass as after.

month.description: YYYY-MM, UTC. Present only when the period is a calendar month (the default, or ?month=).

by_sku.description: GPU time by SKU, sorted by SKU.

jobs.description: Jobs with at least one settle accepted in the month.

by_day.description: One entry per UTC day of the period, in order, zeros included, so a chart has a slot per day. GPU settles only.

by_key.description: GPU settles by the API key the job was submitted with, largest first. GPU settles only.

from.description: First day of the period, inclusive, UTC.

to.description: Last day of the period, inclusive, UTC.

status.description: open until the webhook says otherwise; refunded and partially_refunded follow a refund to the card, disputed and lost a dispute (B2).

receipt_url.description: Stripe's hosted receipt, once the webhook has credited the top-up and the charge was looked up.

bonus_usd.description: Bonus credit this top-up earns (ADR-0013 §1: 3% from USD 50, 5% at USD 100), fixed when it was created and credited with the payment. No cash value; a refund or dispute takes back the same share of it.

refundable_usd.description: What can still be asked back to the card: the amount less refunds and disputes; 0.00 unless the top-up is credited or partially_refunded.

refund_request.description: The open refund request for this top-up if there is one, otherwise the newest, whatever its status.

topups_enabled.description: Whether POST /topups can work in this deployment (Stripe keys set and valid for its environment).

bonus_tiers.description: ADR-0013 §1's tiers, highest first, so the form can show the credit a payment earns before the customer pays.

bonus_usd.description: The bonus credit the payment will add with it; the card is charged amount_usd only.

status.description: open until a refund of the top-up is applied (refunded), the operator declines it, or the customer cancels it.

resolution.description: The operator's message when declined; empty otherwise.

KeyRef.description: The API key a job was submitted with. name and display are empty strings when the key row no longer exists.

status.description: The job's current status, or an empty string if the job row is gone.

settled_at.description: Unix seconds of the job's last settle in the month; the list order.

gpu_seconds.description: Seconds the month's settles added for this job.

next.description: Pass as after to get the next page. Present only when has_more.

Listing.description: A template an account asked to publish (ADR-0012 §2, marketplace.md M2), as its publisher sees it: review state and reason, whether it is listed, how many jobs ran it (never who), and the template as buyers would see it.

review_reason.description: The super admin's reason; absent while pending.

public.description: listed and approved: what buyers see.

template.description: The template as GET /compute/v1/templates would show it, publisher "Unify Compute".

open.description: Whether this deployment serves account listings to buyers (false in production until ADR-0012 §4 holds). Submitting and review work either way.

other_sessions.description: Live sessions of this user other than the caller's.

status.description: expired: can no longer be accepted, still listed for 30 days so it can be sent again

invited_by_email.description: Empty when the inviter has left the account
